question.text: Under SEBI (FPI) Regulations, 2019, which of the following is an eligibility criterion (under Regulation 11.3.1) for a designated depository participant (DDP)?

answer.text: The applicant must be an Authorised Dealer Category-1 bank authorised by RBI under FEMA, 1999
The applicant must be a SEBI registered merchant banker
The applicant must have minimum net worth of Rs. 100 crores
The applicant must be a registered stock broker under SEBI regulations

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the standard DDP eligibility criteria in Regulation 11.3.1, one requirement is that the applicant be an Authorised Dealer Category-1 bank authorised by RBI under FEMA, 1999. The Trap: Merchant banker status, a Rs. 100 crore minimum net worth and stock-broker registration are not part of the standard Regulation 11.3.1 eligibility criteria for a DDP. Note: The workbook also describes a notwithstanding route where SEBI may consider a regulated entity with custodial-services experience that is registered as a depository participant and custodian and has a tie-up with an AD Category-1 bank - so the AD Category-1 bank linkage can be satisfied directly or via a tie-up under that exception.
